text: dsh-load-agent-rules 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的项目规则加载插件。它发现 Cursor、Copilot、Windsurf、Cline、Kiro、Roo、Gemini 和 Junie 的规则文件，并保留规则的始终生效、文件匹配或按需读取方式。始终生效规则进入会话上下文，匹配文件的规则在工具触碰文件后附加，其他规则可由 project_rule 工具读取。插件还提供侧栏设置页，可调整来源和容量等选项，适合希望 DSH 遵循已有项目约定的开发者。规则从本地工作区读取，不需要额外 API 密钥。

dsh-load-agent-rules brings Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, Cline, Kiro, Roo, Gemini and Junie rules into DSH. It keeps always-on, file-scoped and on-demand behavior, with a project_rule reader and sidebar settings. It reads local workspace files; no API key is needed.
让 DSH 读取仓库里现成的 Cursor 和 Copilot 规则。
我想让项目的 AI 编码约定自动进入 DSH 上下文。
DSH 能否根据当前编辑的文件加载对应的规则？
把 Windsurf、Cline 或 Kiro 的项目指引接到 DSH 里。
希望模型需要时能按名称读取一条项目规则。
规则太多时，怎样只把匹配当前文件的约定附给模型？
Load existing coding-agent instructions from my repository into DSH.
Can project rules be attached only when a matching file is touched?
dsh-load-agent-rules 的功能「跨助手规则发现」：支持从八类编码助手约定目录发现规则，解析各自的 front matter，并按内容去重；管理员可通过 sources 配置选择启用哪些来源。
dsh-load-agent-rules 的功能「按文件匹配附加规则」：读取或编辑工具触碰文件时，插件匹配规则中的 glob 范围，并把尚未提供的匹配规则附加到当前步骤上下文。
dsh-load-agent-rules 的功能「始终生效规则与容量控制」：会话开始前将始终生效规则放入指令上下文，并按字节预算保留内容；超出预算的规则列入目录供后续读取。
dsh-load-agent-rules 的功能「按需读取已列出的规则」：模型可调用 project_rule 工具按规则名称读取完整正文；工具返回规则是否找到及其文本。

dsh-load-agent-rules README · dsh-load-agent-rules：Lots of repos already have rules for AI agents, just not in a format DeepSeek Harness reads. Someone on the team wrote `.cursor/rules/testing.mdc`, another person added `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, and there's a `.windsurfrules` from that one month everyone tried Windsurf. DSH reads `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, but it ignores the rest. So the agent never hears "we use Vitest, not Jest" or "never edit old migrations", even though it's written down right there in the repo.
dsh-load-agent-rules README · dsh-load-agent-rules：This plugin finds those rule files and gives them to the model the way each tool meant them to be used. You don't have to convert or copy anything.

dsh-load-agent-rules README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-load-agent-rules
```

That's the `web` profile, the browser UI you start with `dsh web`. If you run DSH another way, use `headless` (scripts and CI) or `acp` (editor integrations) instead. Each profile keeps its own plugin list, so add it to every profile you use. It starts working in the next session. Remove it with `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-load-agent-rules`.

dsh-load-agent-rules README · From a clone：To try local changes, build a tarball and install that:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/acus9345/dsh-load-agent-rules
cd dsh-load-agent-rules
npm install
npm pack

dsh-load-agent-rules README · Which files it reads：| Tool | Files |
| --- | --- |
| Cursor | `.cursor/rules/**/*.mdc` (nested ones in subfolders too), `.cursorrules` |
| GitHub Copilot | `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` |
| Windsurf | `.windsurf/rules/*.md`, `.windsurfrules` |
| Cline | `.clinerules` (file or folder) |
| Kiro | `.kiro/steering/*.md` |
| Roo Code | `.roo/rules/*`, `.roorules` |
| Gemini CLI | `GEMINI.md` |
| JetBrains Junie | `.junie/guidelines.md` |

dsh-load-agent-rules README · Which files it reads：Many repos have the same text under several names, often as a symlink. Duplicates are dropped, and so is anything identical to your `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, since DSH already loads those.

dsh-load-agent-rules README · How rules reach the model：Each of those tools has its own idea of when a rule applies. The plugin keeps those meanings instead of dumping every rule into the prompt.

**Always-on rules** go into context once, at the start of the session. That covers Cursor's `alwaysApply: true`, Copilot's main instructions file, Windsurf `always_on`, Kiro `inclusion: always`, and plain files like `.cursorrules`. If a rule file changes mid-session, or context compaction drops the rules, they're sent again.

dsh-load-agent-rules README · How rules reach the model：**File-scoped rules** wait until they're relevant. A Cursor rule with `globs: "*.tsx"`, a Copilot file with `applyTo: "src/db/**"`, a Kiro `fileMatch` or a Windsurf `glob` rule gets attached the first time the agent reads or edits a matching file. It's attached once, not on every touch. Rules in a nested `packages/web/.cursor/rules/` folder only apply inside `packages/web/`.

dsh-load-agent-rules README · How rules reach the model：**Rules with only a description** (Cursor's "agent requested", Windsurf `model_decision`) are listed by name and description. The model can open any of them with a small `project_rule` tool when it decides one is relevant. Manual-only rules show up in that list too.

So the model's first request carries something like this:

```
These are the project rules written for this repository. Follow them like the rest of your instructions.

dsh-load-agent-rules README · How rules reach the model：<rule name=".cursor/rules/style.mdc">
Use tabs for indentation. Prefer named exports.

dsh-load-agent-rules README · Settings：The easy way: open **Plugins** in DSH's sidebar, click **dsh-load-agent-rules**, change what you want and press **Save**. It applies to the next tool call, no restart needed (`toolName` is the one setting that still needs a restart, so it is not on the page).

Or add a row like this to `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`, or to `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml` for every profile. Keys you leave out keep their defaults.

dsh-load-agent-rules README · Settings：```yaml
- id: load-agent-rules
  config:
    sources: [cursor, copilot, windsurf, cline, kiro, roo, gemini, junie]   # drop any you don't want
    maxBaselineBytes: 48000    # budget for always-on rules; the rest are listed instead

If your always-on rules go over the budget, the ones that don't fit are listed with a note, and the model reads them with the tool. Nothing is silently cut.

dsh-load-agent-rules README · Development：```sh
npm install
npm test           # discovery and rendering unit tests
npm run test:e2e   # real dsh runs against a scripted local model, no API key needed
```

The install test runs `dsh plugin add`, which needs `pnpm` on your PATH.
